newsitem.title: UK: Hopes for durables spree buoys Carpetright.
newsitem.headline: Hopes for durables spree buoys Carpetright.

text.p: Hopes for increased spending on household durables helped spur a rally in Carpetright Plc shares on Tuesday, but analysts had different views on the carpet retailer's longer-term prospects.

The group's four percent increase in like-for-like sales since the start of May reassured the market, which had feared a slowdown, retail analysts said. "Any progress is good news," said one, who asked not to be identified.
The increase was set against very tough comparatives for the same period last year when the retailer achieved a 30 percent jump in sales.
Analysts said the shares, which have dropped steeply from a high earlier this year of more than 600 pence, could recover further.

"If the household related market gets through the budget unscathed the shares should have another leap forward," said Robert Miller at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson. The Labour government's first budget is due on July 2.

Some profit forecasts were held unchanged or nudged upwards to just over 40 million stg, from the high 30s. But concern about the group's ability to sustain gross margins persuaded one analyst to reduce his to 41 million stg from 43 million.
The shares were up 40.5 pence at 481.5 pence by 1330 GMT.
